recipes.name: Angel Hair with Feta and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package tomato basil feta cheese, crumbled
3 ounces sun-dried tomatoes, softened and chopped

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook angel hair pasta in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, 4 to 5 minutes. Drain and return pasta to the pot.
Mix Parmesan cheese, tomatoes, olive oil, and garlic into pasta. Stir in cilantro; season with salt and pepper. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Angel Hair with Feta and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: My husband begs me to make this pasta recipe with sun-dried tomatoes and feta. You’ll love the surprisingly great mixture of flavors.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful - fast and tasty!! I did do a few things differently. I had to double the recipe to feed everyone so I sauted the garlic with some chopped onion in the olive oil until soft. I then added 1 can of low fat chicken broth, a little white wine and both sun-dried tomatoes and some chopped Roma tomatoes and let this simmer while the pasta cooked. The smell was unbelievable! I used fresh basil and tossed in some sliced olives. Tossed all together, and then gently stirred in the cheeses at the last. My son said it was a gourmet meal! We might try throwing in some shrimp or chicken strips next time, although with a salad and some french bread, its a complete, wonderful meal. Thank you for sharing!!

So this was an amazing 5 star pasta recipe that only took 15 minutes to prepare. I did a couple of things differently from the recipe. First of all, I doubled the garlic and minced it. It was actually sautéed in olive oil with the sun dried tomatoes before tossing with the pasta. Regular crumbled feta worked out to be a perfect match. It was shocking to see how well the cilantro paired with this recipe. I strongly recommend this as it will not disappoint!

Yum! so good! Added a can of chicken broth, a little white wine, some fresh basil and some Kalamata olives. Added the cheeses at the end. Used fresh angel hair pasta. Sauteed some chicken breasts in olive oil and garlic and sliced the chicken and served on top of the pasta. So delicious!!!!!

Very easy and versatile. I changed quite a bit up. I used whole wheat thin spaghetti (I like the whole wheat, but there was no angel hair whole wheat pasta available). I used sundried tomato pesto instead of actual sundried tomato. I also used parsley, because I like the taste of it better than cilantro. Finally, I sauteed the garlic then tossed the parsley in it when the oil cooled to just warm. Then I added it all in with the pasta.

Paired with a green salad, this made a satisfying meal for my husband and I. Will definitely make again. I didn't make an entire box of pasta, so just had to estimate amounts of ingredients and made some minor adjustments (as I do with most recipes). However, I believe the recipe would be very tasty as is.

My alterations:
- sauteed red onion (because I had it on hand) and pre-minced garlic (convenience) in 1 T. olive oil, then added sun dried tomatoes before adding pasta. 
- used low-fat plain feta and just added some dried basil to the pasta
- used whole wheat thin spaghetti. It adds a nice nutty flavor and fiber.

I would definitely make it again. I was looking for something light without heavy sauces or meat for a hot summer day, perfect! My husband the meat man liked it too! I used some of the mentioned changes, sautéed onions and garlic, fresh basil and Roma tomatoes as well as sun dried. I also used Asiago cheese in place of feta with the Parmesan.

Fabulous dish! It was very simple and very good. I could have made a meal out of this all by itself! I doubled the amount of sun-dried tomatoes and used regular feta cheese. I also used fresh basil instead of cilatro. This dish can easily be modified to suite your tastes. It can be served warm or cold. I found I really enjoyed it better the next day and added some red pepper flakes, kalamata olives and a splash of balsamic vinegar. No matter what you do it's bound to be delicious - especially with a nice glass of wine!
Great pasta dish! I added 2/3 cup oil cured black olives and 1/4 c sliced scallions. My husband and I both loved this dish. I will make this again.

THIS WAS FANTABULOUS!! This is the best pasta dish I have ever made! I sauteed green onions, garlic, sundried tomatoes with their own oil, basil, about 4 tblsp. of chicken broth until liquid almost absorbed. Then I mixed pasta with the sauteed mixture, added shredded Italian cheese mix,(mozzarella,parmesean,) then added crumbled basil/tomatoe feta, not too much it is salty. This was absolutely the best dish ever, the whole family loved it! I served it with grilled chicken strips. We will definitely add this to our recipe box and will make it often. MMMM MMMM Good!

I thought this was great. I cooked the onion etc a bit before blending. I also added a few tomatoes and olives. I think I would prefer basil over cilantro. The cilantro wasn't bad but it just wasn't quite right for this meal. I will make this again. 2nd time I added chicken broth, grilled chxn, and grape tomatoes and made a simmer sauce. I used 1/2 cup of feta and a few splashes of oil. Topped with some deli peppercini peppers and they were good. Just used some dry basil, no cilantro.

This recipe is so yummy!! I used jarred sun-dried tomatoes in oil (used the oil from the jar instead of olive oil), artichoke hearts, fresh basil and parsley (instead of cilantro), and Greek olives. Like other reviewers I sauteed the garlic and tomatoes and waited until the very end to add the feta. Definitely a keeper! Thank you!

I like this recipe, but the hubby found it OK. I did not use the cilantro as it seemed more appropriate to add Italian parsley or even fresh basil. I will try it next time by adding some protein such as tuna and capers or just the capers. It is mildly flavored so I would say it is a recipe that is good for tweaking it until you find the best combo to make it into an outstanding one! Still, it is fast and easy to make and the flavor is mild good for a quick meal! I might try again but will get creative for sure!

This was easy to make but it seemed to be missing something - it was a bit bland. Not that it was bad just missing something. I definitely wish I would have reserved some pasta water to give it a more saucy texture.
My family loves this! It's a quick and easy weekday meal.
Delicious, easy to make, and if you’re a garlic lover this is the dish for you!

This was tasty, however I modified by using reserved pasta water to stir in with the added ingredients. I omitted cilantro and used basil instead. I recommend using of each added ingredient to balance the 16 oz of pasta.
Amazing recipe and tastes very much like restaurant quality! Subbed the olive oil for butter and added black olives and capers but other than that made the recipe as written. Delicious!

This was good as written. Both my wife and I thought it was missing something that would make this even better. By looking at other peoples pictures, our sun dried tomatoes looked different. There's looked more like what my wife and I were thinking would help this recipe. We though like chunks of tomatoes or something else like that. I will make it again and try some other things in it.
Really good flavour and easy.
This is a great recipe. I did not change a thing. It's a nice change from tomato sauce. I will definitely be making this again!
